docs.summary: This class is responsible for managing the audio context.

Raised immediately before the device is closed, while everything built from it is still valid. Release native objects here rather than after the fact: once the context is gone, so is the node graph they are attached to, and uninitializing them then is a use after free.
Converts a world position, direction or velocity into the space the audio engine works in.
docs.remarks: Prowl is left handed with +Z forward, the audio engine is right handed with -Z forward, so the two disagree by a mirror on one axis. Mirroring the vectors that cross the boundary is what gets all three axes right. Mirroring one of the listener's basis vectors instead (negating its world up, say) also lines left and right back up, but it does it by flipping the handedness of the basis, which leaves vertical inverted.

docs.summary: True once a device is up. False before [`Initialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioContext~Initialize), after [`Deinitialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioContext~Deinitialize), if the device failed to open, and for the whole of a headless run. Nothing may be handed to the native layer while this is false.

Bumped every time a device is opened or closed. Anything caching a native object built against the device compares this to know whether its handle is still the current one or a dangling pointer from a previous device.
Gets the chosen sample rate.

docs.summary: Stops the device without closing it, freezing everything that is playing exactly where it is. Set it for a pause menu, clear it to pick every voice up where it left off.
docs.remarks: Silencing the master volume instead would leave the mix running, so a game coming back from a pause would find its music part way past where it stopped. Play mode being paused suspends the device too, and the two are tracked apart, so the editor resuming cannot clear a suspension the game asked for or the other way round.

docs.summary: True while the device is stopped, for either reason.
The elapsed time since last call to 'Update'.

members.name: Initialize
members.signature: public static void Initialize(UInt32 sampleRate, UInt32 channels, UInt32 periodSizeInFrames = 2048, DeviceInfo deviceInfo = null)

docs.summary: Initializes MiniAudioEx. Call this once at the start of your application.

params.sampleRate: The sample rate to use. Typical sampling rates are 44100 and 48000.
params.channels: The number of channels to use. For most purposes 2 is the best choice (stereo audio).
params.periodSizeInFrames: Buffer size for audio processing. This value is a 'hint' so in practice it may be different than what you passed.
params.deviceInfo: If left null, a default device is used.

members.signature: public static void Restart(UInt32 sampleRate, UInt32 channels, UInt32 periodSizeInFrames = 2048, DeviceInfo deviceInfo = null)

docs.summary: Reopens a running device with a different format or on a different output. Does nothing if the settings already match, and nothing at all if no device is open. Opening the first one is [`Initialize`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioContext~Initialize)'s job.
docs.remarks: Everything the old device owned is invalid afterwards, which is what [`DeviceGeneration`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioContext~DeviceGeneration) exists to tell the rest of the engine. Decoded clip data is not device owned and survives untouched. The no device case is not an oversight. Project settings are applied from paths that never wanted audio, headless builds and dedicated servers among them, and reopening had no way to tell those apart from a real format change.

docs.summary: Closes the device and opens it again on the same settings. For picking a device back up after it has stopped underneath the engine, which [`Restart`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioContext~Restart) will not do because nothing about the settings has changed.

members.name: FindDevice
members.signature: public static DeviceInfo FindDevice(string name, int index = -1)

docs.summary: Finds a playback device by the name it reports, falling back to a position in the list. Null if neither finds one.
docs.remarks: Names are what survive between two runs. An index is a position in whatever the backend enumerated this time, so plugging in a headset renumbers the devices after it and a setting saved as an index quietly comes back pointing at a different output.

docs.summary: The buffer size the device was opened with, in frames.
Index of the device in use, or -1 for the system default.

Name of the device in use, empty when the system default was taken. This is what to persist for a "remember my output" setting, since [`DeviceIndex`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Audio.AudioContext~DeviceIndex) only means anything against the enumeration it came from.

Closes the device. Clip data outlives it: those are plain allocations the clips themselves own by reference count, and freeing them here left every live AudioClip holding a dangling pointer, which is also what made reopening the device impossible.
Used to calculate delta time and move messages from the audio thread to the main thread. Call this method from within your main thread loop.

The playback devices the system reports, empty if it reports none. Walking them asks the backend to enumerate the system's hardware and allocates an object per device and per format each one supports, so this is not something to call every frame.
